# Block 7: Data cleaning and validation with AI {.unnumbered} Cleaning mistakes are silent: a missing-value code treated as a measurement, the same animal kept twice, a row quietly dropped. In this block an agent writes and runs the whole cleaning script from one command, and one test run tells you whether to trust it. You own the facts (the codebookA table describing each variable: its type, valid range, missing-value codes, unit and label mappings. It is the data dictionary from Day 2 with machine-readable rules, and you own it, not the AI.); the procedure and the checks ship with the template. *⏱ ~50 minutes* :::{.callout-important} ## Where this fits: same repository, new data file You keep working in the **same workshop repository** as Blocks 4–6, with the `AGENTS.md` you edited in Block 5 and the deny rules you tested in Block 6. What is new is the data file. `data/raw/voles_raw.csv` holds the same 72 voles as `voles_metabolism.csv`, but as they might arrive from the person who collected them: with missing-value codes, inconsistent labels, a mass in the wrong unit and duplicate rows, all planted by your instructor. Every file this block needs is already in your repository; nothing needs downloading. The cleaned file you make here is used only in this block. Blocks 9 and 10 return to `voles_metabolism.csv`. ::: ### Files for this block {#block7-files} **Shipped with the template.** These have been in your repository since you forked it in Block 4. You run or read them; you do not create them. | File | Written by | Its job | Used in | |---|---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_raw.csv` | Your instructor (the voles data with planted errors) | The raw data; never edited | Every step | | `docs/data_note.md` | The data provider (simulated) | Codes, units and valid ranges. The agent is denied reading it | [Step 2](#step-2) | | `scripts/00_profile.R` | Course team | Counts what is in the raw file | [Step 1](#step-1) | | `.agents/skills/clean-with-codebook/` (and its copy in `.claude/skills/`) | Course team | *How* to clean: never touch raw data, log every change, never drop a row silently | [Step 3](#step-3) | | `scripts/functions/validate_voles.R`, `scripts/02_validate.R` | Course team, from the agreed codebook | Validation rules, run on the raw and the clean data | Step 3 (the skill runs them); [Going further](#going-further) | | `tests/test_cleaning.R`, `tests/fixtures/raw_checksum.txt` | Course team, from the agreed codebook, before any cleaning code existed | The one test run that decides whether to trust the cleaning | [Steps 0](#step-0) and [4](#step-4) | | `scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R` | Course team | Summarises the cleaning log for you to read | [Going further](#going-further) | | Deny rules in `.claude/settings.json`; `.gitattributes` | Course team (you read them in Block 6) | Keep the agent's edit tools off the files above; stop git changing the raw file, and so its checksum | Step 0 | **Created in this block.** | File | Created by | Step | |---|---|---| | `docs/profile.csv`, `docs/profile_labels.csv`, `docs/profile_ids.csv` | You, by running `00_profile.R` | 1 | | `docs/codebook.csv` | The agent drafts it; you correct it and save it | 2 | | `scripts/01_clean.R` | The agent, through the skill | 3 | | `data/derived/voles_clean.csv`, `cleaning_log.csv`, `exclusion_log.csv` | `01_clean.R`, when it runs | 3 | Short of time at any step? The `block7-done` branch holds a codebook, `01_clean.R` and its three outputs. The cleaning and the checks both read the codebook but never each other, so a misunderstanding in one is caught by the other: :::::::: {.dia .dia-lanes role="figure" aria-label="The cleaning pipeline in order. Facts first: data/raw/voles_raw.csv, pinned by a checksum, is profiled by 00_profile.R into docs/profile.csv and two companion tables; the agent drafts a codebook from the profile; you correct it against the provider's note, docs/data_note.md, into docs/codebook.csv. The voles data have errors planted in them; your instructor holds the answer key, so at the end you measure what your pipeline caught. The steps follow [the safe vibe-coding recipe](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd#safe-recipe) from Block 4. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Background: why not simply ask a chatbot to clean the data? In a 2025 study, language models given polluted tables missed codes such as `-1` (a sentinel valueA number with a special meaning, such as 9999 for “not recorded” or -1 for “run failed”. It must be documented in a codebook and recoded before analysis.) and rarely spotted near duplicates (Spreafico et al., 2025). Those error classes are planted here. ::: ## Step 0: Check the safeguards are in place {#step-0} :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Recipe check (3 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** your workshop repository on `main`, Git pane clean (behind on Block 5? switch to `block5-done` in the Git pane's branch menu; Block 6 adds only a permission rule, so `block5-done` is the right checkpoint). **1. The protections.** Start `claude` and type `/permissions`. Look for these deny rulesA permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code’s built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files., shipped in `.claude/settings.json`: `Edit(/data/raw/**)`, `Read(/docs/data_note.md)`, `Edit(/docs/codebook.csv)` and `Edit(/tests/test_cleaning.R)`. **2. The checks.** In the Files pane, `tests/` holds `test_cleaning.R` and `fixtures/raw_checksum.txt` (a checksumA short fingerprint computed from a file’s contents, for example with tools::md5sum(). Any change to the file changes the checksum, so it detects changes made by any route. of the raw file). Both ship with the template: the course team wrote the tests from the agreed codebook before any cleaning code existed, so they cannot share the cleaning script's mistakes. The tests skip until clean data exist. **You are done when** you have seen the four rules and the two files. **If it goes wrong:** if `/permissions` lists no rules, check you started `claude` from the workshop repository's Terminal tab; if the files are missing, switch to `block5-done`. :::: ::: ## Step 1: Profile the raw data {#step-1} Profiling is counting, so R does it, not the model. `scripts/00_profile.R` ships with the template; it reads `data/raw/voles_raw.csv` and writes three tables to `docs/`: | File | One row per | Shows | |---|---|---| | `profile.csv` | column | missing values, distinct values, numeric minimum and maximum | | `profile_labels.csv` | label in `sex` and `treatment_arm` | how often each spelling occurs | | `profile_ids.csv` | `subject_id` that appears more than once | possible duplicates | :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The shipped `scripts/00_profile.R` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/00_profile.R ---- # Purpose: describe the raw file as entered, before any decision is made. # Every column is read as character so codes such as 9999 or -1 appear # exactly as entered. library(tidyverse) library(here) raw_df <- read_csv( here("data", "raw", "voles_raw.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()) ) # one row per column: missingness, distinct values, numeric range ---- profile_df <- raw_df |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |> # suppressWarnings: text values become NA here by design mutate(value_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) |> summarise( n_rows = n(), n_missing = sum(is.na(value)), n_distinct = n_distinct(value, na.rm = TRUE), n_numeric = sum(!is.na(value_num)), min_numeric = if (all(is.na(value_num))) NA_real_ else min(value_num, na.rm = TRUE), max_numeric = if (all(is.na(value_num))) NA_real_ else max(value_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = column ) # every distinct label in the categorical columns ---- labels_df <- raw_df |> select(sex, treatment_arm) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |> count(column, value, sort = TRUE) # identifiers that appear more than once ---- repeated_ids_df <- raw_df |> count(subject_id) |> filter(n > 1) # print in full, and save each table so it can be opened, pasted or diffed ---- print(profile_df, n = Inf, width = Inf) print(labels_df, n = Inf, width = Inf) print(repeated_ids_df, width = Inf) write_csv(profile_df, here("docs", "profile.csv")) write_csv(labels_df, here("docs", "profile_labels.csv")) write_csv(repeated_ids_df, here("docs", "profile_ids.csv")) ``` ::: ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Profile (5 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("scripts", "00_profile.R")) View(readr::read_csv(here::here("docs", "profile.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)) ``` ::: Every column is read as text, so `9999` and `-1` appear exactly as entered. Look for numbers far outside the rest, labels that differ only in spelling or case (`profile_labels.csv`) and repeated IDs (`profile_ids.csv`). **You are done when** the three profile files exist in `docs/` and you have noted anything that looks odd. **If it goes wrong:** restart R (*Session → Restart R*) and run the line again. :::: ::: ## Step 2: Draft the codebook with the agent, then audit it {#step-2} The codebook is Day 2's data dictionary ([README chapter](06-reproducibility.qmd#repro-fix)) with machine-readable rules. **Why a CSV, not a table in the README?** Code reads it. `01_clean.R` reads `docs/codebook.csv` every time it runs, so the rules are never copied into the script by hand, and the over-cleaning test reads its `min`, `max` and `missing_codes` columns. A Markdown table is for people; a CSV is for people *and* code. **Where the facts come from.** `docs/data_note.md` ships with the template. It stands in for what you would get from whoever collected the data: a methods sheet, a lab-book page or an email. The agent is denied reading it, so it drafts from the profile alone, like an analyst who never asked for the note. That gap is the point of the exercise. :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Draft and audit the codebook (12 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **1. Ask for a draft.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text /plan Draft docs/codebook.csv with the columns column, type, rule, min, max, missing_codes, unit, source, from docs/profile.csv, docs/profile_labels.csv and docs/profile_ids.csv only. In the source column, say for every entry whether it comes from the profile or is your assumption. Show the CSV in your reply; do not write any file. ``` Read rules are best effort: if it proposes a command that would open the note, refuse it. **2. Save it yourself.** `usethis::edit_file("docs/codebook.csv")` in the R console, paste, save. The agent is denied this file: the codebook is yours. (Avoid Excel, which can silently change quoted fields.) **3. Audit the draft.** Before you open `docs/data_note.md`, answer: - Did the draft list `9999` as a missing-value code, or treat it as a large measurement? - Did it notice that `-1` is a code? - Where did its `min` and `max` come from? A range read off the data includes its errors, so valid ranges must come from the biology or the protocol. **4. Correct it against the note.** Open `docs/data_note.md` (also shown below the task) and make every line trace to the note or to a decision you can defend. Where the note gives no unit (metabolic rate), write ``, not a guess: Block 10 relies on it. Commit in the Git pane. **You are done when** `docs/codebook.csv` is committed, with every rule traceable to the note or to your own decision. **If it goes wrong:** if you are short of time, copy the codebook below into `docs/codebook.csv` and commit it; it is what most groups converge on. :::: ::: :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The shipped `docs/data_note.md` (open after step 3 of the task) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` markdown # Data note: vole metabolism experiment From the colony manager who collected the data. One row per animal. - **subject_id**: `V` followed by three digits (for example `V007`). Each animal appears once. - **sex**: `M` or `F`. - **treatment_arm**: `Control`, `Low_dose` or `High_dose`. - **mass_pre_g**, **mass_post_g**: body mass in grams, before and after treatment. Adults in this colony weigh between 15 and 60 g. We entered `9999` when an animal could not be weighed. - **metabolic_rate_post**: metabolic rate after treatment, from the respirometer. Valid readings lie between 5 and 30. We entered `-1` when the respirometry run failed. ``` ::: ::: :::
``` column,type,rule,min,max,missing_codes,unit,source subject_id,character,"pattern ^V[0-9]{3}$; unique; pad digits to three",,,,,data note sex,character,"allowed M, F; recode male to M, female to F",,,,,data note treatment_arm,character,"allowed Control, Low_dose, High_dose; match case-insensitively",,,,,data note mass_pre_g,double,,15,60,9999,g,data note (range from colony records) mass_post_g,double,,15,60,9999,g,data note (range from colony records) metabolic_rate_post,double,,5,30,-1,,data note (range from equipment) ```
## Step 3: Clean with one command {#step-3} The skill holds the procedure; your codebook holds the facts. The skill ships with the template (in `.agents/skills/clean-with-codebook/`, copied to `.claude/skills/`) and runs only when you invoke it by name. It writes `scripts/01_clean.R`, the only new script in this block, and runs the shipped `02_validate.R` and tests. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## What the skill tells the agent (`clean-with-codebook/SKILL.md`) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` markdown --- name: clean-with-codebook description: >- Writes or revises a reproducible R cleaning script that applies a human-authored codebook (docs/codebook.csv) to raw tabular data. Use when asked to clean, recode or prepare raw data in a project that has a codebook. Not for exploratory analysis or modelling. disable-model-invocation: true --- # Clean data against a codebook ## Hard constraints 1. Never modify anything under data/raw/. Read raw files with explicit column types. 2. The codebook is the only source of rules. Do not infer units, ranges, missing-value codes or label mappings that the codebook does not state. 3. Do not edit docs/, scripts/functions/, scripts/02_validate.R, scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R or anything under tests/. If a check fails, report it; never change a check to make it pass. 4. Never drop a row silently. Every excluded row goes in the exclusion log with a reason. 5. Every changed cell goes in the cleaning log. 6. A value outside a codebook range that no codebook rule explains is set to NA, logged with rule "out_of_range_query", and listed in the final report. Never correct it by guessing a unit or decimal error. 7. No imputation. 8. Tidyverse style, native pipe, here::here() for all paths. ## Procedure 1. Present a plan before writing anything: every rule you will apply, the codebook row it comes from, and the order. Wait for the user to confirm. 2. If the data contain a value the codebook does not cover, stop and ask. 3. Write scripts/01_clean.R. It reads docs/codebook.csv when it runs; do not copy rules into the script by hand. Run it in a fresh R session (Rscript scripts/01_clean.R), then run it a second time and confirm the outputs are identical. 4. Run scripts/02_validate.R (raw data should fail, clean data should pass) and every test: Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')". Report both outputs verbatim, including skips. ## Outputs (exact columns) - data/derived/voles_clean.csv: raw_row, then the codebook columns. raw_row is the 1-based row number in the raw file, not counting the header. - data/derived/exclusion_log.csv: raw_row, subject_id (as it appears in the raw file), reason. - data/derived/cleaning_log.csv: raw_row, subject_id, column, old_value, new_value, rule. - rule is one of: missing_code, label_recode, id_format, out_of_range_query. ## Final report Row counts in, out and excluded; every value set to NA for query; any gaps in the codebook you found. ``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Plan, review, then execute (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** the codebook committed and the Git pane showing no changed files. **1. Invoke the skill.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text /clean-with-codebook Clean data/raw/voles_raw.csv using docs/codebook.csv. ``` **2. Review its plan before approving.** Check that: - every rule cites a codebook row; - out-of-range values are set to `NA` and queried, not "corrected"; - no file outside `scripts/01_clean.R` and `data/derived/` will be written; - duplicates are handled by a stated rule, with each exclusion logged. **3. Approve, then read each request.** Choose **Yes, manually approve edits**, an option that appears once the plan is shown. Watch the Git pane: new files should appear only in `scripts/` and `data/derived/`. The skill runs the script twice, then the validation and the tests, and reports the output. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using Posit Assistant Invoke the skill with the same prompt in Normal mode, so it asks before each change; use `/plan` first if you want the plan without any edits. ::: **You are done when** `data/derived/` contains `voles_clean.csv`, `cleaning_log.csv` and `exclusion_log.csv`, and the agent has reported the validation and test output. **If it goes wrong:** if it stalls, loops or writes elsewhere, press `Ctrl+C`, **Revert** in the Git pane, and switch to `block7-done` (a working `01_clean.R` and its outputs). :::: ::: ## Step 4: One check, in a fresh R session {#step-4} The agent says its tests pass: that is a claim. One command, in a fresh R sessionAn R session with nothing loaded from earlier work: Session > Restart R in RStudio or Positron (with “never save .RData” set, as on Day 1), callr::rscript() from the console, or Rscript in the terminal. Code that only works in your current session depends on something you did not record., turns it into evidence. **Where the tests come from.** `tests/test_cleaning.R` ships with the template. The course team wrote it from the agreed codebook (the one in Step 2), before any cleaning code existed, so it checks what the cleaning *should* do, not what one script happens to do. The agent did not write it and cannot edit it: `Edit(/tests/test_cleaning.R)` is one of the deny rules you checked in Step 0. In your own projects, write these tests yourself, from your codebook, before you ask an agent to clean. :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Run the checks (6 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **1. Run every test.** Restart R (*Session → Restart R*), then: **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} callr::r(\(d) testthat::test_dir(d), list(here::here("tests"))) ``` ::: What a pass proves: | Test in `test_cleaning.R` | A pass proves | |---|---| | raw data are unchanged | The raw file still matches its checksum: nothing changed it, by any route | | every raw row is in the clean data or the exclusion log | No row was dropped silently, and every exclusion has a reason | | every log entry is truthful | Each logged old value is the raw value, and each new value is the one in the clean file | | every changed cell appears in the log | No change went unrecorded | | no more values set to NA than the codebook explains | Nothing was over-cleaned | | cleaning is reproducible | A fresh run writes byte-identical files | | clean data pass every codebook rule | The result obeys the codebook | **2. Read the change.** In the Git pane, **Diff** `scripts/01_clean.R` for anything the plan did not mention, then commit the script and its outputs. **You are done when** every cleaning test passes (other blocks' tests may skip) and the work is committed. **If it goes wrong:** a failing test names the problem. Ask the agent to fix `01_clean.R`, quoting the test; never the test itself (it is deny-protected). Short of time? Switch to `block7-done`. :::: :::

to_long(raw_df, "raw_value"), clean_long = to_long(clean_df, "clean_value") ) } test_that("raw data are unchanged", { checksum_path <- here::here("tests", "fixtures", "raw_checksum.txt") skip_if_not(file.exists(checksum_path), "Block 7 Step 0 not done yet") recorded <- readLines(checksum_path) current <- unname(tools::md5sum(here::here("data", "raw", "voles_raw.csv"))) paste("values newly set to NA in", col)) } }) test_that("cleaning is reproducible: a fresh run writes identical files", { skip_if_not(file.exists(clean_path), "Block 7 not done yet: no clean data") = here::here(), show = FALSE) expect_identical(unname(tools::md5sum(derived)), before) }) test_that("clean data pass every codebook rule", { skip_if_not(file.exists(clean_path), "Block 7 not done yet: expect_true(pointblank::all_passed(validation)) }) ``` :::

## Going further (not covered live) {#going-further} This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. ::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The validation rules `scripts/functions/validate_voles.R` was transcribed from the codebook by a person, not by the agent that writes the cleaning script. It uses the pointblank package: each line is one rule, and `interrogate()` reports how many rows break it. (pointblank calls the object that holds the rules an "agent"; it has nothing to do with AI agents.) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/functions/validate_voles.R ---- # Rules transcribed from docs/codebook.csv by a human, not by the agent # that writes the cleaning script. voles_col_types <- function() { readr::cols( subject_id = readr::col_character(), sex = readr::col_character(), treatment_arm = readr::col_character(), mass_pre_g = readr::col_double(), mass_post_g = readr::col_double(), metabolic_rate_post = readr::col_double(), .default = readr::col_character() ) } validate_voles <- function(data, label) { data |> pointblank::create_agent(label = label) |> pointblank::col_vals_not_null(columns = c(subject_id, sex, treatment_arm)) |> pointblank::col_vals_regex(columns = subject_id, regex = "^V[0-9]{3}$") |> pointblank::rows_distinct(columns = subject_id) |> pointblank::col_vals_in_set(columns = sex, set = c("M", "F")) |> pointblank::col_vals_in_set( columns = treatment_arm, set = c("Control", "Low_dose", "High_dose") ) |> pointblank::col_vals_between( columns = c(mass_pre_g, mass_post_g), left = 15, right = 60, na_pass = TRUE ) |> pointblank::col_vals_between( columns = metabolic_rate_post, left = 5, right = 30, na_pass = TRUE ) |> pointblank::interrogate() } ``` ::: `scripts/02_validate.R` runs the rules on the raw data, which should fail (for example `Raw data (expected to FAIL): 7 of 10 rules fail`), and, once the cleaning has run, on the clean data, which should pass. It also lists any value that could not be read as a number: such a value would become `NA` and slip past the range rules. In an interactive session it opens the full report in the Viewer. **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("scripts", "02_validate.R")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/02_validate.R ---- # Runs the codebook rules on the raw data (expected to FAIL) and, once # 01_clean.R has run, on the clean data (expected to PASS). In an interactive # session the full pointblank report also opens in the Viewer. library(tidyverse) library(here) source(here("scripts", "functions", "validate_voles.R")) report_validation <- function(validation) { steps <- validation$validation_set n_failed <- sum(!steps$all_passed) cat( validation$label, ": ", if (n_failed == 0) "all rules pass" else paste(n_failed, "of", nrow(steps), "rules fail"), "\n", sep = "" ) if (interactive()) print(validation) invisible(validation) } raw_df <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "voles_raw.csv"), col_types = voles_col_types()) # values that could not be read as numbers become NA and would pass the # range rules, so list them print(problems(raw_df), width = Inf) report_validation(validate_voles(raw_df, "Raw data (expected to FAIL)")) clean_path <- here("data", "derived", "voles_clean.csv") if (file.exists(clean_path)) { clean_df <- read_csv(clean_path, col_types = voles_col_types()) report_validation(validate_voles(clean_df, "Clean data (expected to PASS)")) } ``` ::: :::{.callout-warning} `na_pass = TRUE` lets genuine missing values through. It would also let through a cleaning script that replaced *every* mass with `NA`. Validation alone cannot catch over-cleaning; the over-cleaning test in `tests/test_cleaning.R` can. ::: :::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Write the validation rules independently Instead of using the shipped `validate_voles.R`, you can have the rules written by an AI that has never seen the cleaning code, for example a browser chat window given only the codebook: **Prompt (browser chat):** ```text Using only the codebook below, write an R file containing a function validate_voles(data, label) that builds a pointblank agent with one validation step per codebook rule, and interrogates it. Also write voles_col_types(), returning readr column types for the codebook columns, with character as the default for anything else. [paste docs/codebook.csv] ``` Compare what it writes with the shipped version. A rule it missed, or a range it took from the data rather than the codebook, is the kind of error the separate conversation is meant to expose. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Read the log yourself The tests prove the log is truthful and complete; they cannot tell you whether a change was the right decision. The shipped `scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R` counts the changes by column and rule, and samples ten logged changes for you to check by eye against the raw file (`View()`, or Positron's Data Explorer). ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("scripts", "03_audit_cleaning.R")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R ---- # Purpose: read the cleaning log yourself. tests/test_cleaning.R already checks # that the log is truthful and complete; it cannot tell you whether each change # was the right decision. That is your job. library(tidyverse) library(here) cleaning_log_df <- read_csv( here("data", "derived", "cleaning_log.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()) ) # 1. What kinds of change were made ---- cleaning_log_df |> count(column, rule, sort = TRUE) # 2. Ten logged changes to check by hand against the raw file ---- set.seed(2026) cleaning_log_df |> slice_sample(n = 10) |> print(width = Inf) ``` ::: ::: ::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The fresh-run checks, one by one The test suite already reruns the cleaning in a fresh R session. To do the same checks by hand, commit the outputs, then in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} renv::status() callr::rscript(here::here("scripts", "01_clean.R")) ``` ::: `renv::status()` should report a consistent state; if the agent used a package that is not in the lockfileThe renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment., decide whether you want it and record it yourself with `renv::snapshot()`, as on [Day 1](01-projects.qmd) (the agent is denied `renv.lock`). After the `callr::rscript()` run the Git pane should show no changes. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## At the command line `Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')"`, `Rscript -e "renv::status()"`, `Rscript scripts/01_clean.R` and `git status --short data/derived`, run after `/exit` or in a second Terminal tab. See [checking work](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#checking-work). ::: :::: ::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## How the template's safeguards were made **The checksum.** The template's `tests/fixtures/raw_checksum.txt` was written once, from the shipped raw file, like this: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_create(here::here("tests", "fixtures")) writeLines( unname(tools::md5sum(here::here("data", "raw", "voles_raw.csv"))), here::here("tests", "fixtures", "raw_checksum.txt") ) ``` ::: Do the same for your own raw data, then commit it. The template's `.gitattributes` contains `data/raw/** -text`, so git does not convert line endings, which would change the checksum on Windows. **The deny rules.** This is the `.claude/settings.json` in your workshop repository, the same file you read in [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` json { "permissions": { "defaultMode": "default", "deny": [ "Edit(/data/raw/**)", "Read(/docs/data_note.md)", "Edit(/docs/data_note.md)", "Edit(/docs/codebook.csv)", "Edit(/scripts/02_validate.R)", "Edit(/scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R)", "Edit(/scripts/functions/validate_voles.R)", "Edit(/tests/fixtures/**)", "Edit(/tests/make_reference.R)", "Edit(/tests/test_cleaning.R)", "Edit(/renv.lock)", "Edit(/.github/**)", "Edit(/.claude/**)", "Edit(/.posit/**)", "Edit(/hooks/**)", "Read(/.Renviron)", "Read(/.env)" ] } } ``` ::: ::: A leading `/` anchors each pattern to the project root. The rules protect specific files rather than whole folders, so the agent can still write `scripts/01_clean.R` and `data/derived/`. To protect files of your own, add rules with `/permissions`. Posit Assistant has no documented path rules for file edits; use the guard hook from the *Going further* section of [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd) instead. :::{.callout-warning} **What each control covers.** The deny rule blocks the agent's file-editing tools, and shell output redirects such as `> file`. It does not cover R code the agent runs: an R script that writes to `data/raw/` is a different route. The checksum test catches a change made by *any* route, but only after the fact. Use both: one prevents, the other detects. A deny rule on reading does not stop data reaching the model provider by other routes; see [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd). ::: **The skill.** The skill ships in `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`. To use it in another project, download it and unzip it into that project's `.agents/skills/` (`unzip(file.choose(), exdir = here::here(".agents", "skills"))`), then copy the folder into `.claude/skills/` with `fs::dir_copy()`. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: :::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
checksum A short fingerprint computed from a file's contents, for example with tools::md5sum(). Any change to the file changes the checksum, so it detects changes made by any route.
codebook A table describing each variable: its type, valid range, missing-value codes, unit and label mappings. It is the data dictionary from Day 2 with machine-readable rules, and you own it, not the AI.
deny rule A permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code's built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files.
fresh R session An R session with nothing loaded from earlier work: Session > Restart R in RStudio or Positron (with "never save .RData" set, as on Day 1), callr::rscript() from the console, or Rscript in the terminal. Code that only works in your current session depends on something you did not record.
lockfile The renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment.
sentinel value A number with a special meaning, such as 9999 for "not recorded" or -1 for "run failed". It must be documented in a codebook and recoded before analysis.
